دَحِيقٌ Driven away; (K;) removed; remote; put away, or far away. (S, K.) ―
-b2- A man removed from good, or prosperity; and from others; as also ↓ مُدْحَقٌ . (TA.) ―
-b3- عَيْنٌ دَحِيقٌ is like مَطْرُوفَةٌ [i. e. An eye hit, or hurt, with a thing, so that it sheds tears]. (Ibn-'Abbád, K, TA. [In the CK, المَطْرُوقَة is erroneously put for المَطْرُوفَة.]) مَنْ عَانَكَ عيْنُهُ دَحِيقْ فِيهَا تُرْبٌ سَحِيقْ وَ دَمُهُ تَدْفِيقْ وَلَحْمُهُ تَمْشِيقْ [Whoso smites thee with an evil eye, may his eye be hit, or hurt, so as to shed tears; may there be in it bruised earth; and may his blood be copiously shed; and may his flesh be much lacerated;] is one of their formulas of incantation. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
